subtitle: Learn the theory and application of 7th, 9th, 11th, and 13th chords in popular music

backLink.label: Back to Chord Theory in Songs

introduction.title: Beyond the Triad
introduction.text: Extended chords add notes beyond the basic triad (1-3-5) to create richer, more sophisticated harmonies. They're the difference between "Three Little Birds" and "Giant Steps" - same harmonic principles, different levels of complexity.

columns.title: Harmonic Sophistication
columns.text: Extended chords provide more colors in your harmonic palette while maintaining clear functional relationships.

columns.title: Voice Leading
columns.text: Additional chord tones create more possibilities for smooth voice leading and melodic bass lines.

columns.title: Genre Flexibility
columns.text: From jazz standards to neo-soul, extended chords adapt to any style requiring harmonic sophistication.

cards.title: 7th Chords
items: C7 (C-E-G-Bb): Dominant function - wants to resolve. Blues, jazz, pop
Cmaj7 (C-E-G-B): Sophisticated major - dreamy quality. Jazz, R&B, neo-soul
Cm7 (C-Eb-G-Bb): Smooth minor - less final than triad. Jazz, funk, R&B
Cm(maj7) (C-Eb-G-B): Mysterious, haunting - rare but powerful. Film scores, art music

cards.title: 9th Chords
items: C9 (C-E-G-Bb-D): Rich dominant - jazz standard. Jazz, blues, R&B
Cmaj9 (C-E-G-B-D): Lush, dreamy - very sophisticated. Jazz, neo-soul, ambient
Cm9 (C-Eb-G-Bb-D): Complex minor - emotional depth. Jazz ballads, R&B
Cadd9 (C-E-G-D): Major with 9th, no 7th - bright and open. Pop, rock, folk

cards.title: 11th & 13th Chords
items: C11 (C-E-G-Bb-D-F): Very dense - often with omitted 3rd. Jazz, fusion
C13 (C-E-G-Bb-D-F-A): Full extended dominant. Jazz, big band
Csus4 (C-F-G): Suspended 4th - creates tension. All genres - very common
Csus2 (C-D-G): Suspended 2nd - open, ambiguous. Rock, pop, ambient

cards.title: Piano/Keyboard
items: Play bass note with left hand, chord tones with right
Use "rootless voicings" - omit the root in right hand
Stack chord tones in 4ths for modern sound
Practice common jazz voicings (shells, drops, etc.)

cards.title: Guitar
items: Learn moveable 7th chord shapes across the neck
Use partial voicings - not all notes need to be played
Focus on the characteristic intervals (maj7, b7, 9th)
Practice chord melody - melody note on top of extended chord

cards.title: Songwriting
items: Start with simple triads, add extensions for color
Consider the melody - avoid clashing with chord extensions
Use extended chords at emotional peaks or resolutions
Balance sophistication with accessibility

cards.title: A Jazz Standard's Sophisticated Harmony

fields.label: Analysis
fields.value: vi7 - ii7 - V7 - Imaj7 (in C major)

items: Am7: Smoother than Am triad, less final
Dm7: Perfect subdominant preparation
G7: Classic dominant 7th - strong pull to I
Cmaj7: Sophisticated resolution, dreamy quality

cards.title: Why Extensions Work Here
items: 7th chords create smoother voice leading
Less finality allows continuous flow
Sophisticated enough for jazz context
Each chord has clear but rich function
Emotional Effect: Romantic, sophisticated, flowing rather than choppy

sections.title: When and How to Use Extended Chords

cards.title: Good Situations
items: Jazz, R&B, neo-soul contexts
Ballads requiring emotional sophistication
When you want smoother voice leading
Bridge sections or climactic moments
Instrumental sections where complexity works

cards.title: Be Careful When...
items: The melody clashes with chord extensions
You're writing simple, anthemic music
The genre doesn't expect sophistication
You're using them just to show off
The arrangement is already busy

cards.title: Jazz/R&B Standards
items: ii7 - V7 - Imaj7 (classic resolution)
Imaj7 - vi7 - ii7 - V7 (circle progression)
vi7 - bII7 - Imaj7 (tritone substitution)
iii7 - vi7 - ii7 - V7 (descending)

cards.title: Pop/Rock Applications
items: Imaj7 - V7 - vi7 - IV (sophisticated pop)
vi7 - IVmaj7 - I - V7 (ballad progression)
Isus2 - Isus4 - I (resolution motion)
I - Isus4 - vi - IVadd9 (modern pop)

exercises.title: Beginner Practice
items: Learn basic 7th chord shapes in all keys
Practice ii7-V7-Imaj7 in multiple keys
Add 7ths to familiar chord progressions
Practice sus2 and sus4 resolutions

exercises.title: Advanced Practice
items: Learn rootless voicings for piano
Practice 9th, 11th, and 13th chords
Reharmonize pop songs with extended chords
Study jazz standards for extension usage
